 The United States will end daylight saving time at 2 a.m. on the 1st (local time). As a result, the New York stock market’s opening and closing times in Korea will each be pushed back by one hour: it will open at 11:30 p.m. and close at 6 a.m. the following day. Agence France-Presse (AFP) / Yonhap News Agency 
The United States will end daylight saving time at 2 a.m. on the 1st (local time). As a result, the time difference between New York and South Korea will widen from 13 hours to 14 hours.
 New York stock market trading hours will also be pushed back by one hour from their current times.
 The regular session will open at 11:30 p.m. Korea time and close at 6 a.m. the following day.
 The premarket session will run from 6 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. Korea time, while after-hours trading, following the close of the regular session, will run from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m. the next day.
 Every year, the United States starts daylight saving time at 2 a.m. on the second Sunday in March, as spring arrives, and ends it at 2 a.m. on the first Sunday in November, in autumn.
